description: An eight-panel composite figure that mixes two property plots with six EBSD-derived maps. (a) plots true stress sigma (left axis, MPa) and strain hardening rate dsigma/depsilon (right axis, MPa) against true strain (0.0–0.6) for M1-IA (black) and M2-IA (red); the dash-dot curves are dsigma/depsilon with marked points A and B, the solid curves the flow stress. (b) plots retained austenite (vol.%, 0.0–0.5) versus true strain with printed exponential fits f_gamma = 45.6*e^(-3.6*epsilon) for M1-IA and f_gamma = 19.6*e^(-3.8*epsilon) for M2-IA. (c,d) are EBSD phase maps (legend: red = ferrite, green = austenite; 5 µm scale bar) after tensile testing, annotated f_gamma = 6.5% (M1-IA) and f_gamma = 3.2% (M2-IA). (e,g) are KAM maps before and (f,h) after tensile testing for M1-IA and M2-IA respectively, with a colour bar Min 0 (blue) to Max 5 (red) and 5 µm scale bars. Arrows label delta-ferrite in (g) and dashed ellipses label strain partitioning in (h). The figure links the mechanical TRIP signature in (a,b) to the microstructural proof in (c–h).
measured_quantities: kernel average misorientation KAM (degrees, scale Min 0 to Max 5)

observations.observation: Panel (a) carries two ordinate axes in MPa: left for true stress sigma and right for strain hardening rate dsigma/depsilon, plotted against true strain from 0.0 to 0.6, with a legend distinguishing M1-IA (black) and M2-IA (red).

In panel (a) the strain hardening rate curves (dash-dot) fall steeply from high values at low strain and then run nearly flat while the solid true-stress curves keep rising; two markers A (triangle, M1-IA) and B (square, M2-IA) sit on the hardening-rate curves.
No numerical values are printed on the hardening-rate curves; the MPa values at points A and B are given only in the citing text (1338 MPa for M1 and 989 MPa for M2).
Panel (b) prints two exponential fits for the decay of retained austenite with true strain: f_gamma = 45.6*e^(-3.6*epsilon) for M1-IA and f_gamma = 19.6*e^(-3.8*epsilon) for M2-IA.

The retained austenite curves in (b) start at about 0.45 vol.% axis fraction for M1-IA and about 0.20 for M2-IA near zero strain and decrease monotonically to roughly 0.06 and below 0.02 respectively at the highest plotted strain.
The phase-map legend above panels (c,d) defines red as Ferrite and green as Austenite.
Panels (c) and (d) are annotated with f_gamma = 6.5% and f_gamma = 3.2% respectively, and both maps are almost entirely red (ferrite) with only sparse green (austenite) after tensile testing.
The caption states that (e,g) are KAM maps before and (f,h) after tensile tests, for M1-IA (e,f) and M2-IA (g,h).
The KAM colour scale shared by panels (e–h) is labelled Min 0 to Max 5, running from blue through green and yellow to red.

Panels (e) and (g) (before testing) are dominated by low-KAM blue, whereas (f) and (h) (after testing) show a much larger fraction of green-yellow-red high-KAM area, indicating a clear increase in local misorientation after deformation.
In panel (g) dashed arrows point to relatively featureless regions labelled delta-ferrite, and in panel (h) dashed ellipses mark regions labelled Strain Partitioning.
The citing text states that austenite fractions before tensile testing were 45% (M1) and 19% (M2), falling to 6.5% and 3.2% after testing, which is taken as evidence of the TRIP effect.
The citing text attributes stage-II of the strain hardening rate curves to deformation-induced martensite transformation of austenite (TRIP) and stage-III to void formation before necking.

The citing text refers to the KAM maps as 'Fig. 11c-f', which conflicts with the panel labels (e–h) visible in the figure and with the caption; the citation's panel letters are inconsistent with the image.

subfigures.description: Dual-axis plot: true stress sigma (left, MPa) and strain hardening rate dsigma/depsilon (right, MPa) versus true strain 0.0–0.6, with legend M1-IA (black) and M2-IA (red). Solid curves are flow stress, dash-dot curves the hardening rate; black triangle A and blue square B mark the end of the gradual hardening-rate decline on the M1-IA and M2-IA curves.

Retained austenite (vol.%, 0.0–0.5) versus true strain (0.0–0.6) for M1-IA (black) and M2-IA (red), both decaying monotonically; printed fits f_gamma = 45.6*e^(-3.6*epsilon) and f_gamma = 19.6*e^(-3.8*epsilon).
EBSD phase map of M1-IA after tensile testing, dominated by red (ferrite) with sparse green (austenite); annotated f_gamma = 6.5%; 5 µm scale bar.
EBSD phase map of M2-IA after tensile testing, also almost entirely red (ferrite) with very little green; annotated f_gamma = 3.2%; 5 µm scale bar.
KAM map of M1-IA before tensile testing; predominantly dark blue (low misorientation) with scattered green, 5 µm scale bar.
KAM map of M1-IA after tensile testing; markedly higher KAM, appearing as mottled green-yellow texture, 5 µm scale bar.
KAM map of M2-IA before tensile testing; mostly blue with dashed arrows pointing to regions labelled delta-ferrite, 5 µm scale bar.
KAM map of M2-IA after tensile testing; high-KAM green/yellow/red network with dashed ellipses and a label 'Strain Partitioning' indicating coexisting low- and high-KAM regions, 5 µm scale bar.

unreadable_items: The exact tick values along the true-strain and right-hand MPa axes of panel (a) are only partly legible at the supplied resolution
The very fine green (austenite) regions in the post-test phase maps (c) and (d) are too small to quantify visually; the reported f_gamma values are read from the printed annotations
Panel-by-panel fine structure of the KAM maps (e-h) cannot be resolved quantitatively; only the 0-5 colour scale is readable
